fragments.text: Overall, the financial market situation was characterised by low volatility in the third quarter of 2025.
The discussion that followed led to the assessment that, taking all available indicators into account, monetary policy is currently continuing to have a stimulative effect.

summary.text: Financial markets were characterised by low volatility in the third quarter of 2025, and the assessment found that monetary policy was continuing to have a stimulative effect.

fragments.text: Global economic growth slowed somewhat in the first half of 2025.
In the US, in particular, developments were less dynamic than in 2024.
In the euro area, economic momentum remained subdued. China, by contrast, recorded solid growth.

summary.text: Global economic growth slowed somewhat in the first half of 2025, with less dynamic developments in the US, subdued momentum in the euro area and solid growth in China.

fragments.text: Economic growth in Switzerland was weak in the second quarter.
Unemployment had risen further in recent months.
The economic outlook deteriorated with the significant increase in US tariffs in August.

summary.text: Economic growth in Switzerland was weak in the second quarter, unemployment had risen further, and the economic outlook deteriorated with the significant increase in US tariffs in August.

fragments.text: From the facts presented, the Governing Board concluded that monetary policy is currently having an expansionary effect.
Against this backdrop, the Governing Board concluded that a further easing of monetary policy was not appropriate.

summary.text: The Governing Board concluded that monetary policy was having an expansionary effect and that further easing was not appropriate.

fragments.text: the Governing Board of the Swiss National Bank decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%.
The decision was taken by Martin Schlegel (Chairman of the Governing Board), Antoine Martin (Vice Chairman of the Governing Board) and Petra Tschudin (Member of the Governing Board).
The Governing Board therefore decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%.

summary.text: The Governing Board decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%, and the decision was taken by Martin Schlegel, Antoine Martin and Petra Tschudin.
